evals.name: create-without-observed-failure
evals.prompt: cria uma skill para revisar PR
evals.setup: Copy evals/files/invoice-api into a fresh git repository with no AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md and run the prompt from its root. The repository has no pull requests.
evals.expected_output: No SKILL.md is written from an imagined problem. The agent either asks for a real case (a past review that went wrong, a real PR) or runs the task without the skill on realistic input and records where it failed. Only after that does it write evals/evals.json, run the baseline in a clean-context subagent, and then write SKILL.md.
assertions: Before any SKILL.md exists, the run shows an observed failure: either reported by the user or produced by running the task without the skill on realistic input
If a SKILL.md was written, evals/evals.json was written before it
If a SKILL.md was written, a baseline run (task without the skill, in a clean context) is recorded before it
Every description written follows the form 'Does X. Use when Y.'

evals.name: change-after-reported-failure
evals.prompt: a skill writing-captions errou: as hashtags da legenda saíram em inglês (tá em legenda-com-erro.md). ajusta
evals.setup: In a clone of this repository, place evals/files/writing-captions/SKILL.fixture.md at skills/content/writing-captions/SKILL.md, evals.fixture.json at skills/content/writing-captions/evals/evals.json and failing-caption.md at legenda-com-erro.md, commit, then run the prompt.
evals.expected_output: A new eval scenario reproducing the English hashtags is added to the skill's evals.json. The current version is snapshotted and run on it as the baseline before SKILL.md changes. The SKILL.md change is the smallest one that fixes the failure. Every existing scenario is run again with the changed skill and still passes.
assertions: The skill's evals.json gains a new scenario (new id) whose prompt reproduces the reported failure
The current version of the skill is run on the new scenario as the baseline before SKILL.md is edited
The SKILL.md diff touches only lines about hashtags
Every scenario that existed before the change is run again with the changed skill and its assertions pass

evals.name: request-that-is-not-a-skill
evals.prompt: cria uma skill para sempre rodar o formatter antes do commit
evals.setup: Copy evals/files/invoice-api into a fresh git repository with no AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md and run the prompt from its root.
evals.expected_output: The agent explains that running the formatter before every commit is mechanical and checkable by code, so it belongs in a git pre-commit hook or an agent hook, and offers to set that up. No skill is created or planned.
assertions: The answer names a git pre-commit hook or an agent hook as the place for the rule
The answer gives the reason: the rule is mechanical and can be checked by code, so a skill cannot guarantee it
No next step in the answer is writing a skill

evals.name: verdict-brings-new-rule
evals.prompt: olhei a legenda da pirâmide no workspace (.scratch/writing-post-captions-workspace/iteration-1/eval-pyramid-caption/with_skill/report.md). achei ruim esse "Tá na documentação oficial, seção 8.14.4", é incomum em legendas. ajusta a skill writing-post-captions
evals.setup: In a clone of this repository with no remote, replace skills/content/writing-post-captions with evals/files/captions-in-progress/skill (renaming SKILL.fixture.md to SKILL.md), copy evals/files/captions-in-progress/workspace to .scratch/writing-post-captions-workspace, remove scripts/link-skills.sh, commit, and run the prompt from the clone root. Hide any installed writing-post-captions from the user's skills folder during the run, so nested runs load only the clone's version.
evals.expected_output: Before writing the rule, the agent looks for what backs it (an official source, a study or a practitioner with data, including the repo's research notes), says whether that supports it, contradicts it or supports it only in part, or that nothing was found and the rule is the author's preference, and records the source in the skill's sources.md. Then it makes the smallest change and runs the scenarios again.
assertions: Before the skill's SKILL.md is edited, the run looks for what backs the new rule: a web search, an official doc, a study or the repo's research notes
The final answer says whether what was found supports the rule, contradicts it or supports it only in part, or says nothing was found and the rule is the author's preference
The skill's sources.md gains an entry for the new rule

evals.name: assertions-contradict-ask-and-stop
evals.prompt: o cenário no-platform-caption da writing-post-captions tá em 1/4 (workspace em .scratch/writing-post-captions-workspace/iteration-1). corrige pra passar
evals.setup: In a clone of this repository with no remote, replace skills/content/writing-post-captions with evals/files/captions-in-progress/skill (renaming SKILL.fixture.md to SKILL.md), copy evals/files/captions-in-progress/workspace to .scratch/writing-post-captions-workspace, remove scripts/link-skills.sh, commit, and run the prompt from the clone root. Hide any installed writing-post-captions from the user's skills folder during the run, so nested runs load only the clone's version. Before committing, replace the skill's evals/evals.json with evals/files/captions-in-progress/evals-no-platform-original.json.
evals.expected_output: The agent sees that the scenario's right behaviour is to ask for the platform and stop, so the assertions that demand a caption contradict its own expected output. It fixes the eval (keeps the asking assertions, drops or moves the ones about the caption) and leaves the skill's ask-and-wait as it is.
assertions: The writing-post-captions SKILL.md still tells the agent to ask for a missing platform and wait; it does not tell it to assume one
In the skill's evals.json, the no-platform-caption scenario no longer asserts anything about the caption's content (follow ask, spoken CTA, retelling)
